In Postgres, x IS NOT NULL is normalised to NOT x IS NULL. sqlglot should keep IS NOT NULL as written, represented as an exp.Is whose negate flag is set, while NOT x IS NULL stays as written too; the Postgres shorthands NOTNULL and ISNULL should read as IS NOT NULL / IS NULL, IS NOT UNKNOWN as IS NOT NULL, and constant folding in the optimizer must respect the negation (NULL IS NOT NULL simplifies to FALSE).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("SELECT r IS NOT NULL FROM t", read="postgres").sql("postgres")
# currently: SELECT NOT r IS NULL FROM t
# expected:  SELECT r IS NOT NULL FROM t

parse_one("r IS NOT NULL", read="postgres").args.get("negate")
# currently: None
# expected:  True

parse_one("SELECT r NOTNULL FROM t", read="postgres").sql("postgres")
# currently: SELECT NOT r IS NULL FROM t
# expected:  SELECT r IS NOT NULL FROM t
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.

In Postgres, x IS NOT NULL is normalised to NOT x IS NULL. sqlglot should keep IS NOT NULL as written, represented as an exp.Is whose negate flag is set, while NOT x IS NULL stays as written too; the Postgres shorthands NOTNULL and ISNULL should read as IS NOT NULL / IS NULL, IS NOT UNKNOWN as IS NOT NULL, and constant folding in the optimizer must respect the negation (NULL IS NOT NULL simplifies to FALSE).

For example:

```python
from sqlglot import parse_one, transpile, exp

parse_one("SELECT r IS NOT NULL FROM t", read="postgres").sql("postgres")
# currently: SELECT NOT r IS NULL FROM t
# expected:  SELECT r IS NOT NULL FROM t

parse_one("r IS NOT NULL", read="postgres").args.get("negate")
# currently: None
# expected:  True

parse_one("SELECT r NOTNULL FROM t", read="postgres").sql("postgres")
# currently: SELECT NOT r IS NULL FROM t
# expected:  SELECT r IS NOT NULL FROM t
```

Other forms of the same constructs described above should work as well.
